5.  Almost every human adult unknowingly hosts these microscopic creatures within their facial pores and hair follicles. They primarily survive by consuming the natural oils and dead cells that accumulate in these areas, particularly around the nose, cheeks, and eyelashes. Research has suggested that while they are generally harmless, their populations can increase with age and may be linked to certain skin irritations like rosacea. Name this genus.
